title: AI Calculators and Interactive Decision Tools

reading.body:
Six interactive estimators cover the questions that decide whether an AI project is viable: token cost, GPU memory, context window fit, training cost, energy and carbon, and return on investment.

The set is organized around constraints rather than capabilities. GPU memory and context window fit are hard limits, and a project that exceeds either does not run at all. Token cost and training cost are the recurring and one-time bills. Energy and carbon sit alongside them as a physical input rather than an afterthought. Return on investment is the only one that asks whether the result is worth the spend.

For AI specifically, the pairing matters. Compute capacity and power draw are the same question asked at different layers, and these tools let a reader move between them without leaving the arithmetic. Each estimator shows its own work and states what it excludes, which is the honest form for a model that cannot capture every variable.

What the data does not cover is the estimators themselves. It names six and describes none of their inputs, formulas, or error ranges. It also gives no worked examples, no comparison between estimates and measured results, and no indication of how often the numbers hold. A reader learns that these questions are the ones that decide viability, not how well any tool answers them.
